title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-20
content:
Purpose: capture commands, error snippets, quick hypotheses while debugging the 8k+ seqlen KV cache / attention kernel mismatch that led to degraded outputs and occasional segfaults on dedicated nodes.

Context: after bumping default max_seq_len to 8192 for some long-context customers, we started seeing: occasional integrity-check failures in the KV cache (len mismatch), degraded perplexity at long sequences for some models, and 1-2 segfaults/week on dedicated GPU pools running the optimized attention kernels. Issue appears correlated with key/value caching + flash-attn-like kernel selection for certain layer shapes.

Observed symptoms (timeline):
- 2026-02-20: first alert from canary for redwood-v2-7b-long: model outputs truncated / hallucinating after ~4k tokens in a handful of requests (customer CS ticket RDW-1123).
- 2026-02-22: SRE reports 1 segfault on dedicated-pool-a (NVIDIA H100) while serving a long chat (seqlen ~6.5k).
- 2026-02-24: Reproduced in unit test harness (see commands below) with deterministic seed leading to KV cache length mismatch error in runtime assert: "KVCache::get_len() != kv_len (layer 9)"

Commands / test harness runs tried:
1) Baseline reproduce (local bench harness):
   PYTHONPATH=./python ./bench/long_context_test.py --model redwood-v2-7b --seq-len 8192 --batch 1 --seed 42 --enable-kv-cache
   - Result: intermittent assert: "KVCache::get_len() != kv_len (layer 9)" after ~1200 tokens generated.

2) Kernel logging enabled (runtime flag):
   RUNTIME_LOG_KERNEL_SELECTION=1 PYTHONPATH=./python ./bench/long_context_test.py --model redwood-v2-7b --seq-len 8192 --batch 1 --seed 42 --enable-kv-cache
   - Output (snippet):
     [kernel-select] layer=9 seq_len=8192 qk_dim=64 choose_kernel=flash_attn_v2
     [kernel-select] layer=10 seq_len=8192 qk_dim=128 choose_kernel=generic_attn_fallback
     [kernel-select] layer=9 post_kv_cache_len=4096 (unexpected)
   - Hypothesis: kernel selection logic and the KV cache stride/packing code disagree on effective cached length for some layers (maybe due to quantization stride rounding).

3) Run with "force-generic" kernel flag:
   PYTHONPATH=./python ./bench/long_context_test.py --model redwood-v2-7b --seq-len 8192 --batch 1 --enable-kv-cache --force-kernel=generic_attn
   - Result: no assert in 10 runs (till 8192 tokens), latency higher but stable.

4) Run with smaller per-layer kv-block-size tweak (PATCH_LOCAL):
   export KV_BLOCK=32 && PYTHONPATH=./python ./bench/long_context_test.py --model redwood-v2-7b --seq-len 8192 --enable-kv-cache
   - Result: reduced frequency of assert, still see mismatch in ~1/15 runs.

5) Stress test on dedicated pool (replay of customer trace):
   ./tools/replay_trace.sh --trace-id rdw-longtrace-20260220 --concurrency 4 --model redwood-v2-7b --kv-cache
   - Observed 2 segfaults over 3 hours. Core dumps show crash in flash_attn kernel codepath (cuBLAS/cuDNN stack frames).

Error snippets / logs (raw):
- Runtime assert: "KVCache::get_len() != kv_len (layer 9)"
- Kernel warning: "flash_attn: packed_kv_stride % 64 != 0, falling back"
- CUDA error: "unspecified launch failure" at flash_attn.cu:2314
- Trace snippet (heap): "kv_cache_ptr=0x7f8b1d000000 total_len=8192 expected_stride=2048 actual_stride=1984"

Immediate hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Packing/stride calculation bug when using quantized weights (INT8/4-bit) + specific layer dim combos (qk_dim not divisible by block), leading to miscomputed packed_kv_stride. Kernel selects flash-attn assuming packing alignment that runtime kv-cache doesn't satisfy -> index ofs mismatch -> assert/segfault.
- Hypothesis B: Race between KV cache population and kernel selection in multi-threaded warmup path (rare interleaving). But unit test runs single-threaded and still reproduced -> lower priority.
- Hypothesis C: Memory reuse bug in per-layer allocator when kv-block-size changes dynamically (autoscaling adjustments).

Quick checks to validate hypotheses:
- Re-run with quantized model disabled (use fp16 model): reproduces? -> NO reproduction in 20 runs. Points to quantization interaction.
- Force kernel selection to generic_attn -> stable. Points to flash-attn path.
- Instrument packing calc: add assert that expected_stride % 32 == 0 and log per-layer qk_dim, kv_block_size. Found layer 9 qk_dim=96 kv_block_size=31 -> mismatch.

Patch ideas / next steps:
- Short-term mitigation: force-generic for models with long default seqlen + quantized configs (deployable via config flag per-model). Patch PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/pull/482 (WIP).
- Medium-term fix: unify packing/stride calc between runtime and kernel selector. Add unit tests for all qk_dim x kv_block_size combos up to 256. Add an assert in kernel-selection stage to check runtime packing assumptions before choosing flash-attn.
- Long-term: make flash-attn tolerant to non-ideal strides or update quantization packing to round up to kernel-friendly strides (and pad KV cache accordingly).

Notes / breadcrumbs:
- Reproducible locally with seed 42 but still flaky. Use --race-free and --deterministic flags in harness to reduce noise.
- Customer footprint: only a handful of customers use 8k default seqlen + quantized weights; prioritize mitigation for them.
- Differential tests to add: compare outputs with generic vs flash-attn for first 8k tokens to detect subtle drift early (not just crashes).

PRs and people:
- PR WIP: infra/pull/482 (force-generic per-model flag + config) -> owner: Aisha Patel.
- Kernel selection refactor TODO: assign to Ravi Menon (follow-up).
- Ping @infra-oncall and @model-oncall when enabling long seqlen for additional customers.

TODOs (short checklist):
- [ ] Merge hotfix to force-generic for affected model tags (Aisha)
- [ ] Add stride/pack unit tests in runtime (Jordan)
- [ ] Add pre-kernel-selection assert and safe-fallback (Ravi)
- [ ] Run dedicated-pool replay for 24h after patch (SRE)
- [ ] Update runbooks and customer-facing note template (CS)

Small dump of debug commands (for personal recall):
- gdb attach: gdb --args ./bin/serve --model redwood-v2-7b --port 8080
- repro harness: python -m bench.long_context_test --model redwood-v2-7b --seq-len 8192 --seed 42 --log-kernel
- extract core: python tools/extract_core.py --core core.12345 --out stacktrace.txt

Misc notes (brain-dump):
- Might be related historically to change in PACK_STRIDE_ALIGN in commit 9f3a2d (2025-11) where we moved from 32->64 alignment to optimize bandwidth. Re-check that commit for rounding logic.
- Look at quantize_pack() routine in quantization.cc for off-by-one when rounding up to stride.
- Also check per-layer override code path used by Dedicated config (we sometimes set kv_block_size smaller to reduce memory) -> could create misaligned strides.

If I forget: ping Aisha, ask for the infra/pull/482 branch and test on staging-dedicated-3 (H100) with the customer trace rdw-longtrace-20260220.

End of scratchpad.
